scope: Entire original finite implication CNR3 and OneChar imply PropGK. RNC16 supplies CNR3; the literal OneChar arithmetic theorem remains an explicit antecedent.

findings.detail: The quotient is cyclic whenever a faithful coefficient character exists. All complex characters with the same kernel are coprime powers of that very character and hence are realized over the same O; cardinality is phi(index), including index1. Without such a witness the universal complex orbit may be empty and remains bounded by phi(index).

Compared the literal twelve fields of GD. Coprime powers preserve character order, the quadratic primary component, parity and the prime-to-ell character kernel, so the eta condition is unchanged. All field/level/prime fields are retained. ell=3 is not excluded by a new guard; its gen antecedent is impossible.

findings.topic: Frobenius, scalar towers and fixed data
findings.detail: Arithmetic Frobenius acts by q on prime-to-p roots of unity, giving cls_N=q and epsilon=q. At sigma^-1, z=chi(q)^-1 gives exactly q^-e*psi(q)^-1+1+q^e*psi(q), the original OneChar scalar. Every closure, prolongation and coefficient isomorphism is chosen after NN.

findings.topic: Exact OneChar use and finite product
findings.detail: The original Selmer length and its normalized real form are retained. Universal trace separation is obtained from singleton admissible collections before OneChar selects finite pairwise-nonisomorphic sets. These sets are reindexed by the entire coefficient/complex-orbit bijection. Repetition across different characters is permitted and remains indexed.

Compared PropGK and the original propGK implication. Taking logarithms of positive nonzero factors gives sum Vn<=2*padicValInt(ell,NN); finiteness is proved before normalized length is used. Constants depend only on K and NN precedes every later coefficient datum. Non-imaginary-quadratic K uses c=A=0,NN=1 and the impossible GD antecedent. The exact finite B task closes; OneChar/RIG_II arithmetic producers do not.
